messages:
maria (support): Jake from Acme reports repeated mid-stream SSE disconnects on iOS 16/17 when toggling WiFi->Cell. Says sometimes response 'stops' and reconnect returns a new stream starting from the beginning (duplicate tokens). Shared logs attached.

customer_jake: repro steps iOS: open chat, send prompt, after ~4–12s toggle wifi off, wait ~3s, toggle back on. Client shows 'connection lost' then reconnects and stream restarts from scratch. We see partial answer twice and final result trimmed. No 401s.

maria (support): Shipping logs show stream closed with code 1001 then subsequent new SSE handshake 200 accepted. No 5xx. Token usage looks normal.

kevin (mobile-eng): Thanks — is the client using the iOS SDK or raw URLSession? Also does the client use HTTP/1.1 event-stream or a WebSocket fallback?

customer_jake: using our wrapper around URLSession with "text/event-stream" Accept header. We do a manual reconnect on reachability change.

olivia (sre): Pasted snippet from proxy logs: 
```
[2026-03-02T14:22:05Z] conn=abcd1234 client=10.1.2.3 "GET /v1/streams?session=xyz" 200 OK; keepalive idle=5s
[2026-03-02T14:22:12Z] conn=abcd1234 -> TLS read error: connection reset by peer (errno 54)
[2026-03-02T14:22:12Z] stream closed normally, code=1001 client-initiated
[2026-03-02T14:22:13Z] new conn=efgh5678 client=10.1.3.4 "GET /v1/streams?session=xyz" 200 OK; new-session
```
Looks like client TCP reset after network handoff, and the client immediately opens a fresh SSE request which our backend treats as a new session (no resume).

kevin (mobile-eng): On iOS URLSession, when network changes the OS can tear down the socket; the SDK needs to implement event-stream idempotency and resume. We don't currently include an explicit resume token in the stream protocol.

maria (support): Customer asks if Redwood can deliver partial tokens buffered prior to reset or support resume.

sam (oncall): Short term: suggest client implement dedup by keeping last token-id and dropping duplicates. Medium term: we can advise adding a resume token param (session_id + last_event_id) and server-side resume logic.

kevin (mobile-eng): Repro code snippet from the app: 
```swift
let task = session.dataTask(with: req) { data, resp, err in
  // parse event-stream progressively
}
// on reachability change we call:
task.cancel()
startNewTask()
```
Cancelling the task triggers a normal close; on reconnect we create a fresh session.

olivia (sre): A few suggestions:
1) Set SSE reconnection backoff and retain last-event-id in client. If server supports Last-Event-ID header, the client can pass it to request resumption.
2) For immediate mitigation, increase our idle keepalive ping to 15s (currently 5s) for mobile clients so short handoffs don't look like idle closes.
3) We can add short lived session tokens so that multiple connections with same session_id are stitched for ~2s to avoid duplicate restarts.

maria (support): Customer wants steps to reproduce from our side and a checklist for them. I'll list what we've done and what we need.

kevin (mobile-eng): Repro on our test device: run app, start stream, trigger airplane mode for 1–3s, re-enable. Observed: OS drops socket -> our client cancels -> server logs connection reset -> new stream starts -> duplicate prefix.

maria (support): Proposed support checklist to send to Jake: 
- Confirm client uses Last-Event-ID or can capture token offsets (example: message sequence numbers).
- If using SDK: update to non-cancel reconnect logic (let socket error then reconnect with last-event-id).
- Temporarily increase client-side reconnect debounce to 1.5s to avoid immediate double reconnections.
- Share a HAR-like capture (server request headers) or proxy logs showing the GET and new GET within 2s.

customer_jake: We can try Last-Event-ID approach. Do you have an example request header?

kevin (mobile-eng): Example curl to test resumption: 
```
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
     -H "Last-Event-ID: 12345" \
     "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/stream?session=xyz" --no-buffer
```
Server should respond with events starting after 12345 if resume supported. We don't currently support Last-Event-ID semantics, so that will be a roadmap item.

olivia (sre): For short-term platform-side changes I'm going to open a ticket: 
- increase keepalive ping for mobile-labeled clients
- add a 2s grace-window to stitch sequential connections from same session_id
- add logging to surface duplicate prefix patterns so support can detect easy cases

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: mobile-sse-keepalive-bump -> canary at 2026-03-03T02:00:00Z (UTC). :rocket:

maria (support): Response to customer with repro checklist, and we'll keep this thread updated after canary.

sam (oncall): FYI, if you need emergency rollback we have the runbook: 
1) revert canary deployment
2) disable stitching feature flag
3) ask client to force-close sockets and retry

customer_jake: Thanks all — we'll try the client changes and send logs. Appreciate the temporary canary. :thumbsup:

maria (support): Marking as "waiting on customer". Will reopen if they confirm failure after client changes.

kevin (mobile-eng): Follow-up note: for mobile UX, consider buffering partial tokens locally and de-duplicating on reconnection using sequence ids. We can provide a small snippet for the iOS SDK if Jake wants it.
